significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) graded and predictive coupling—"the leak is graded with familiarity and largest when the model recognizes the entity but lacks the specific fact, predicting familiarity-driven hallucination"—plus a form-(ii) mechanism in which an identifiable component causally carries that leak and can be steered. This would fix expectations for false claims across familiarity/knowledge cells and connect the entity-recognition signal studied in Do I Know This Entity? (2024) with the truth representations studied in The Geometry of Truth (2023), explaining when recognition-related hallucination specifically arises through truth inflation rather than merely failed recall; it therefore establishes both a substantial phenomenon and a causal mechanism. The claim is determinate, and a verified-negative result would meaningfully rule out recognition-to-truth contamination as that explanation, although it would not rule out other routes from familiarity to hallucination. Topic-substitution check: deleting the specific graded coupling, recognized-but-unknown peak, and causal carrier leaves only the generic topic of LLM beliefs, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the "per-claim recognition-to-truth leak," supplemented by "retrieval gating when recognition is high but knowledge is low" and "abstention calibrated on leak magnitude." It is explicitly ex ante because the leak is "read before any query" to predict associated hallucination, providing an action window for auditors or deployment practitioners rather than only post-hoc explanation. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive graded relation and leak–hallucination predictive coupling would still specify what to expect, although the hypothesis does not clearly guarantee transfer to closed or much larger models and expressly notes that such transfer may fail. Topic-substitution check: LLM-belief research alone supplies none of this predictor, gating rule, or lead time, so the reach derives from claim-specific handles rather than the topic.
